subject: Dedicated footprint allocation & SKU hedging for Argonaut Systems renewal
messages:
From: Tim Liao <tim.liao@argonautsys.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@argonautsys.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal sizing — what should we reserve vs hedge?

Hi Grace,

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off our renewal planning for Argonaut and want to lock down the dedicated capacity footprint for Q1–Q2 next year. Our usage has been spiky (large batched reranking jobs and some long-context research prompts) — attached is a small telemetry snapshot (Q3) and an MVP sizing sheet from my infra team.

High-level ask: we’d like your recommendation for a reserve vs burst plan and the SKU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) to cover the workload while keeping costs reasonable. Also curious about fallback strategies if reserved capacity isn’t fully available right away.

Can you point us to a proposal by EOD next week? Procurement will need a ballpark as they start the internal PO.

Thanks,
Tim
Head of ML Infrastructure
Argonaut Systems

Attachments: telemetry_snapshot_Q3.pdf (summary), argonaut_mvp_sizing.xlsx (workload sample)

Tim — thanks for the data, this is exactly what we need to build a pragmatic recommendation. I’ve looped in Jordan (deal lead) and Irene (dedicated ops) to give an ops-side sizing, and Karthik from product to validate quantization/throughput assumptions.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- Jordan/Irene will draft a 3-tier SKU plan (reserve core, burst pool, cold fallback) with the recommended H100 / A100 / L4 mix and token economics.
- Karthik will validate model packing and quantization options (FP16/4-bit) that affect memory requirements.
- I’ll assemble the package and give you a commit recommendation and a short runbook for fallbacks.

I expect a first-pass PDF by Tue (23 Nov). If procurement needs numbers sooner we can provide a conservative ballpark today: assume 30% H100, 50% A100, 20% L4 by slot-hours for a medium-long context workload profile. That’s high-level and we’ll refine.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Tim Liao <tim.liao@argonautsys.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated footprint proposal (first pass) — Argonaut Systems

Hi all,

Per Grace’s note, attached is a first-pass recommendation based on the telemetry you provided. Key points up top:

1) Workload characterization
- 40% long-context research queries (avg 8k tokens, many KV-cache warmups)
- 35% mid-sized generation (1k–2k tokens) for product features
- 25% high-volume embeddings/rerank (short tokens but high QPS)

2) SKU mix (reserve-first baseline) — rationale
- H100: reserve ~30% of committed GPU-hours for long-context models that need large GPU memory and bandwidth (model sharding or larger per-device batch). H100 gives the best perf for long sequences and quantized FP16/INT8 mixed kernels.
- A100: reserve ~45% for the bulk of generation traffic — good balance of memory and throughput at lower cost than H100. Strong option when you can use tensor-slicing and multi-instance packing.
- L4: reserve ~5% and allocate ~20% to burst/cold pools. L4 is highly cost-effective for embeddings and small-context reranking; it should also serve as fallback for low-latency, stateless requests.

3) Headroom & hedging
- Commit a conservative baseline (60–70% of observed peak token-hours) and keep a burst-capacity plan for 25–30% of expected spikes. This reduces wasted committed spend while protecting SLOs.
- Maintain a short-term burst pool of A100/L4 capacity that can be auto-attached; use H100 only as a warm reserve for scheduled heavy experiments.

4) Fallback strategy
- Prefer model-variant fallbacks: if H100 is unavailable, route inference to an A100-batched variant with smaller context window and an early-exit policy. For embeddings, route to L4; degrade response size or use cached prefixes.

5) Cost/latency tradeoffs (ballpark)
- H100: +35–60% cost vs A100 for the same token throughput on long sequences, but 20–40% lower latency for >=8k token requests.
- A100: best mid-range cost-per-token for general generation.
- L4: 50–70% cheaper for embed/rerank; not suitable for >4k sequences without aggressive tiling.

Attachments included: argonaut_sku_mix_firstpass.pdf (breakdown) and argonaut_mvp_sizing.xlsx (Tim’s original sample annotated).

Irene will add operational constraints (slot preemption policies, autoscale warm pools) and Karthik will follow with quantization notes by EOD.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachments: argonaut_sku_mix_firstpass.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Tim Liao <tim.liao@argonautsys.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint proposal (first pass) — Argonaut Systems

Tim / team — quick operational summary and concrete recommendation for procurement:

Operational constraints we validated
- H100 availability: recommended to reserve as a small committed pool (20–35% of commit) because H100 inventory is constrained in some zones; use cross-region routing as fallback for non-latency-critical jobs.
- A100 autoscale: mature and cheaper to burst; we recommend a managed burst contract that allows up to 40% additional A100 capacity for 90 days during spikes.
- L4: recommend keeping L4 as a burst/cold fallback with auto-attach; set strict request-routing rules to avoid long-context requests on L4.

Concrete procurement numbers (Q1 baseline — monthly committed GPU-hours):
- H100: 1,200 slot-hours/month (reserve) — covers roughly 30% of long-context steady-state.
- A100: 1,800 slot-hours/month (reserve) — bulk of generation.
- L4: 300 slot-hours/month (reserve) + burst pool up to 1,000 slot-hours for embeddings spikes.

Suggested contractual language for PO:
- 12-month commitment with quarterly review and a 20% replenishment clause for burst windows.
- SLA: 99.5% slot availability for reserved pools; burst fulfillment best-effort with 24–48 hour notice for guaranteed higher priority.

Runbook highlights (short):
- If reserved H100 slot shortage occurs: auto-failover to A100 with context clipping and pre-signed fallback flag; notify Argonaut via Slack channel #argonaut-ops.
- For embedding QPS surges: auto-scale L4 burst pool; if L4 saturates, route to cached responses and synthetic throttles.

Next steps
- Grace: confirm if Argonaut wants the conservative baseline numbers in the PO now or prefers a “placeholder commit” and to finalize sizing after two weeks of additional telemetry sampling.
- Tim / Procurement: let us know internal approval timeline and whether cross-region fallbacks are permitted.

Irene Choi
Director, Dedicated Operations — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
